The retrieved literature does not establish a standard taxonomy matching all requested distinctions. A useful proposed annotation scheme separates immediate choice, deferred relevance, explicit mismatch, redundancy, and unidentified-item/insufficient-information abstention. These are operational labels, not established user traits; compatibility, ownership, quantity needs, and mood require explicit evidence. Annotation research emphasizes separating procedural noise from meaningful disagreement ([Kraus & Kroll, 2025](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/34950)). For this study, use independent annotation, evidence spans, per-label counts, agreement statistics, and adjudication; report abstention and usable-evidence coverage separately rather than counting unknown items as dislikes.

For mechanism diagnosis, [Oh & Cho (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722) introduce a recency-bias metric and report improved recommendation performance after mitigation. This motivates controlled history probes: remove recent versus older interactions with matched deletion counts, perturb ordering, and measure paired target-score/rank changes while holding candidate items fixed. These proposed probes measure model sensitivity; they do not establish users’ causal preferences or identify a responsible network layer without component-specific ablations. Pair broad topical-relevance judgments with specific-item suitability judgments to distinguish general relevance from actionable choice.

[Pereira et al. (RecSys 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.05398) show that exposure and candidate sampling can distort offline comparisons, evaluating separability, fidelity, robustness, and alignment with ground truth. Keep the pinned validation evaluator unchanged; treat full-catalog recommendations and qualitative feedback as complementary diagnostics. Twenty training users support exploratory, category-specific hypotheses with explicit denominators and uncertainty, not population-level trait claims.
